changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: For membership businesses: lead with involuntary churn, not the feature. Example: 'Some of your churn is members who never meant to leave. Send us a month of failed renewals and we'll show you which ones were recoverable.' Run this own-data analysis as a standard business-case step before the contract goes to finance, and put the result in front of the signer (for example, the controller), not only the digital lead.
changes.why: Recovery was the message that landed, but only once it was shown on the customer's own file ('Their file, not our average.'). The contract had sat with the controller for two weeks and was signed four days after the data session.

changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For studio and membership prospects, stop leading with unified online-plus-in-store until we can show the reader working live inside the prospect's studio management software. Sell online membership billing as phase one, and position the front desk as a later phase that depends on a partner integration.
changes.why: The unified pitch was heard as 'is that the readers?'. The prospect then asked to see the reader inside their own studio software, saw only the partner's demo, and the front desk stayed out of scope with phase two undated.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For membership businesses operating in one or two countries, do not open with the global positioning slide. Open with the involuntary-churn framing from the M10 change instead.
changes.why: The rep opened with the global slide and got 'Silence.' from a business with studios in the US and a handful in Canada.

changes.change: For finance stakeholders at prospects switching from an incumbent: add a prepared answer on contract term, termination fees and the cost to get out of the incumbent, and raise it before finance asks.
changes.why: The prospect asked 'what's the contract term, what does it cost to get out', the controller asked about termination fees twice, and the incumbent countered with a longer contract. We have no messaging line that addresses exit cost.
